bigpic.b: Wall Street's best week since April 2025
bigpic.t: as chipmakers and Anthropic lead a half-day rally, while state support lifts Seoul and Shanghai by more than 4%.

bigpic.b: OPEC+ meets Sunday with Brent near $95
bigpic.t: and is expected to hold output targets through March, even as Iraq presses for a bigger quota.

bigpic.b: Washington tightens its grip on Southeast Asia
bigpic.t: proposing tariffs of 20% on Singapore and 18% on Malaysia, as Kuala Lumpur tells firms to shun blacklisted chip buyers.

stories.h: Wall Street books its best week since April 2025 as chipmakers lead a half-day rally
stories.sum: The S&P 500 rose 1.60% to 7,297.49 on Friday, the Nasdaq 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow 1.18% to 50,774.94 in a session cut short for Black Friday. For the week the S&P gained 5.6%, the Nasdaq 6.7% and the Dow 5.5%, the Dow's best week since October 2022.
stories.why: The rebound eases pressure after November's AI sell-off, though Goldman warns systematic funds could sell about $100B more.

stories.h: Kospi jumps 4.3% as Seoul weighs a bigger market stabilisation fund
stories.sum: The Kospi rose 204.47 points, or 4.34%, to 4,915.68 on Friday, led by SK hynix, up 5.41%, and Samsung Electronics, up 4.55%. Foreign investors bought a net 1.13 trillion won of shares. Authorities plan a meeting next week on expanding a 10 trillion won stabilisation fund, and Japan's Nikkei gained 2.11% to 58,711.11.
stories.why: Pledges of state support in Seoul and Beijing are steadying Asian chip stocks after a sharp November sell-off.

stories.h: China's CSI 300 has its best day since 2024 as Beijing leans on the national team
stories.sum: The CSI 300 jumped 4.17% to 4,063.06 and the STAR 50 15.07% on Friday after a State Council meeting under Premier Li Qiang urged Central Huijin to act as a market stabiliser and pushed listed firms toward bigger dividends and buybacks. A chip sub-index rose 19%, its biggest gain on record.
stories.why: Explicit state backing could put a floor under Chinese stocks after tech-heavy boards lost roughly half their value since July.

stories.h: Anthropic jumps 11% to $91.88, closing back above its $83 IPO price
stories.sum: Anthropic shares gained 10.98% on Friday, their first close above the $83 IPO price after two sessions below it and a Wednesday low of $73.85. The stock debuted on Nasdaq on 19 Nov. Up to 303M more shares can be sold from 15 Dec, and it is due to join the Nasdaq 100 on 21 Dec.
stories.why: Trading in the biggest AI listing is a running gauge of whether investors will keep funding the sector's huge spending plans.

stories.h: Nvidia pauses Southeast Asia server shipments while it checks export compliance
stories.sum: Nvidia told partners including Dell and Super Micro to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the FT reported, possibly only while they work through new US licence rules for the region. None of the three companies commented. The rules aim to close routes Chinese firms are believed to use to obtain AI chips.
stories.why: Southeast Asia's data-centre build-out relies on steady Nvidia supply, so a long pause could stall projects and their financing.

stories.h: China Mobile and China Telecom open AI hardware tenders that could top 55B yuan
stories.sum: China Mobile's 20 Nov tender covers 52,160 AI accelerator cards, about 2.5 times the volume of its first batch in September. China Telecom's 16 Nov tender seeks 5,248 AI servers and related equipment with a bid ceiling of 25.8B yuan. Together the purchases could exceed 55B yuan, about $8.2B, Caixin reported.
stories.why: China's state carriers are shifting spending from networks to computing, making them some of the country's biggest buyers of AI hardware.

stories.h: 10-year Treasury yield jumps to 4.94% as traders price two Fed hikes by March
stories.sum: The 10-year yield rose 9 basis points to 4.94% in Friday's shortened session as stocks rallied, leaving it little changed on the week. Traders have fully priced two quarter-point Fed hikes by March 2027. The dollar index ended near 104 after its longest run of weekly gains since January 2025, and gold climbed to $3,668.50 an ounce.
stories.why: Higher long-term yields push up mortgage and corporate borrowing costs just as the Fed prepares to tighten again.

stories.h: Brazilian bank stocks surge after Lula picks Bradesco's chairman as finance minister
stories.sum: Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi, 75, Bradesco's chairman and former chief executive, accepted Lula's offer to replace Dario Durigan as finance minister in January. The Ibovespa jumped 6.07% to 176,799.84 on 26 Nov as Bradesco rose 11.6% and Banco do Brasil 12.6%. On Friday, US-listed XP rose 18.07% and Bradesco 15.23%.
stories.why: Investors see a market-friendly finance minister easing fiscal worries, and Brazil's long-term swap rates fell more than 50 basis points.

stories.h: ECB's Nagel says rates may need to rise again as consumers' inflation fears jump
stories.sum: Bundesbank chief Joachim Nagel said on 27 Nov that euro zone inflation could stay above 3% well into 2027 and the ECB might have to do more when it meets in December. An ECB survey showed consumers' 12-month inflation expectations rose to 3.5% in October from 3.1%, and the three-year gauge to 3% from 2.9%.
stories.why: A third ECB hike this year on 17 Dec would lift borrowing costs for euro zone households and firms alongside a likely Fed move.

stories.h: Trump-linked crypto token WLFI plunges 50% to record lows
Bitcoin hovers near $60,000 even as Wall Street has its best week in over a year
stories.sum: Bitcoin traded around $60,100 on Saturday morning in Asia, down 1.84% over 24 hours on CoinMarketCap data, after slipping below $60,000 late Friday in New York despite briefly topping $61,000. Ether was near $1,668. About $7B of options expired on Friday, and US spot bitcoin ETFs have lost a record $5.39B in November.
stories.why: Crypto's failure to join the equity rebound suggests fresh money is staying away, with fund outflows the heaviest on record.

stories.h: US bitcoin reserve bill reaches the House calendar with little time left to pass
stories.sum: H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act, was placed on the House calendar on 24 Nov, two months after a 28 to 21 party-line committee vote. It would have Treasury set up a reserve within 180 days, funded only by seized bitcoin, and bar sales for 20 years. Polymarket gives a 4% chance of a reserve law this year.
stories.why: Without passage before this Congress ends on 3 Jan, the reserve rests on an executive order a future president could reverse.

stories.h: Switzerland's first spot bitcoin ETF starts trading on the SIX exchange
stories.sum: BIT Asset Management listed BBIT on the SIX Swiss Exchange on 26 Nov, seeded with 350 bitcoin worth over $20M and charging 0.19% a year. Swiss regulator FINMA approved it on 20 Oct after an 18-month review and exempted it from diversification rules. BIT says it is Europe's only active spot bitcoin ETF.
stories.why: A regulated ETF wrapper gives Swiss wealth managers a simpler route into bitcoin, even as US funds see record outflows.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price, gaining Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Sanofi shares slipped 1.6% on Friday after gaining nearly 18% over five sessions.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: FDA clears Genentech's giredestrant pill for early breast cancer after surgery
stories.sum: The FDA approved giredestrant, sold as Wilserdly, on 23 Nov for stage I to III ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer at intermediate or high risk of recurrence. In the lidERA trial, 92.4% of patients were free of invasive disease at three years versus 89.6% on standard hormone therapy. A combination use in advanced disease was cleared on 16 Nov.
stories.why: It is the first new hormone drug for early breast cancer in about two decades, opening a large market to oral SERDs.

stories.h: Bayer pays $150M upfront for Hansoh's cancer drug in a deal worth up to $3.25B
stories.sum: Bayer licensed global rights outside Greater China to HS-20122, an early-stage antibody-drug conjugate that targets both EGFR and c-MET in solid tumours including lung cancer. It pays $150M upfront and up to $3.1B in milestones, plus tiered royalties. The deal, announced on 25 Nov, still needs antitrust clearance.
stories.why: Western drugmakers keep turning to Chinese labs for cancer drugs, and antibody-drug conjugates are among the most sought-after assets.

stories.h: OPEC+ set to hold output targets through March as Iraq pushes for a bigger quota
stories.sum: Three sources told Reuters the group has agreed in principle to keep first-quarter 2027 targets unchanged when ministers meet online on Sunday. Iraq says it can pump 5.2M barrels a day against a December quota of about 4.43M, and a preliminary capacity review puts it near 4.9M. The UAE left OPEC and OPEC+ in May.
stories.why: Capacity reviews will set 2027 baselines, so quota disputes could test the group's cohesion months after the UAE's exit.

stories.h: Brent settles at $95.44 for its first weekly gain in November as Gulf attacks persist
stories.sum: Brent fell 1.2% on Friday to $95.44 a barrel but rose about 3% on the week, ending a losing streak, while WTI slipped 0.7% to $83.08. A deadly strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery and Houthi claims of an attack on Ras Tanura kept supply fears alive, and Hormuz traffic ran at about 54% of pre-war levels, Kpler data show.
stories.why: Strikes on Saudi plants and Iran's threats over Hormuz keep a risk premium in crude as OPEC+ meets on Sunday.

stories.h: Taiwan votes on reviving nuclear power as chipmakers' electricity demand climbs
stories.sum: Voters decide on Saturday whether Taiwan should return to nuclear power, which could bring the Maanshan and Kuosheng plants back online; the last reactor shut in May 2025. The KMT-backed measure passes only if yes votes beat no and reach 5,000,959, a quarter of the electorate. Polls close at 4pm, with results due tonight.
stories.why: Chipmakers' power use topped 4.5B kWh in September, up 11.55%, so a yes vote could ease supply strains on TSMC and AI data centres.

stories.h: Stellantis adds December shutdowns at three French plants as Chinese rivals gain
stories.sum: Stellantis will pause Mulhouse and Sochaux on several days in early December, then shut them from 23 and 19 Dec to 11 Jan; Rennes stops from 18 Dec to 5 Jan. About 500 temporary jobs go at Sochaux as a night shift ends in January. Its October registrations in Europe fell 8% to 144,786.
stories.why: Europe's biggest carmakers are trimming output rather than closing plants as cheaper Chinese brands take share and energy costs climb.

stories.h: Toyota bets on a range-extended Highlander to revive its sliding China sales
stories.sum: GAC Toyota set the Guangzhou Auto Show on 27 Nov for the debut of Toyota's first range-extended EV, a Highlander-based SUV. Toyota's China sales fell about 19% to roughly 1.05M vehicles from January to September, with monthly sales down year on year for eight straight months. Nikkei has reported plans for about 200,000 range-extended cars in 2027.
stories.why: Foreign carmakers are adopting Chinese-style range extenders to win back buyers lost to local brands in the world's biggest car market.

stories.h: Battery EVs take 25% of new car sales in Europe this year, and 31% in October
stories.sum: Battery-electric cars made up 25% of registrations across the EU, Norway and Iceland from January to October, up seven points, ICCT data show, and 31% in October alone. Shares reached 32% in France and 29% in Germany but just 8% in Italy and 5% in Poland. Combustion-only cars fell nine points to 28%.
stories.why: Faster EV uptake lets most carmakers meet EU CO2 targets, though ICCT warns the incentive to keep pushing may then fade.

stories.h: Black Friday online spending tops $9.7B by evening, on course to beat Adobe's forecast
stories.sum: US shoppers spent $9.7B online through 6:30pm ET on Black Friday, up 12.8% from a year earlier, Adobe said, putting the day on track for $13.0B to $13.4B against its $12.9B forecast. Salesforce projected US online sales of $18.7B for the day, up 4%. Adobe expects a record $15.1B on Cyber Monday.
stories.why: Online demand is beating forecasts, though with inflation at 3.8%, real growth is thinner than the headline figures suggest.

stories.h: Japan Tobacco shares rise 4% on report it may join a bid for Imperial Brands
stories.sum: Japan Tobacco rose 4.1% to 5,754 yen on Friday after Bloomberg said it is weighing a bid for Imperial with a partner. Altria said it may make an all-cash offer, sending Imperial up 14.85% to 3,432p on Thursday. Under UK takeover rules Altria must bid or walk away by 24 Dec; Imperial says it has had no approach.
stories.why: A two-buyer carve-up could reshape global tobacco, though Japan Tobacco is also absorbing an $8.7B loss on seized Russian units.

stories.h: Sunrise on the Reaping tops Thanksgiving with $11.6M as Focker-in-Law edges Hexed
stories.sum: Lionsgate's Hunger Games prequel took $11.6M on Thanksgiving Day and is projected to earn $85M over five days, lifting its domestic total to about $233M. Universal's Focker-in-Law made $7.7M and is tracking $40M, ahead of Disney's Hexed at $4.5M and $34.4M. Hexed cost more than $200M to make.
stories.why: A weak start for Disney's costly original adds pressure on studios' non-franchise bets in a key holiday window.

stories.h: Skydance clears near-term Warner Bros. Discovery debt and registers PIPE shares
stories.sum: Skydance ended a $4B receivables facility on 20 Nov and will redeem about $709.5M of 2027 notes in late December, leaving roughly $168M due next year. It also registered for resale about 3.9B non-voting shares sold for $47B to fund the Warner Bros. Discovery deal, locked up until 4 Apr 2027. Total debt is about $16.1B.
stories.why: Clearing near-term maturities buys the merged studio time, but debt of about 4.6 times earnings keeps pressure on cost cuts.

stories.h: Netflix buys Los Angeles's 1928 Radford Studio Center for a reported $380M
stories.sum: Netflix said on 24 Nov it is purchasing the Studio City lot and will keep the existing studio team. The 55-acre site was bought for $1.85B in 2021 by Hackman Capital Partners and Square Mile Capital before falling into foreclosure, so the reported price is a steep discount.
stories.why: Owning a historic lot cheaply secures Netflix production space in Los Angeles as distressed studio property changes hands.

stories.h: Norse Atlantic's Norwegian airline files for bankruptcy after losing its 787 fleet
stories.sum: Norse Atlantic Airways AS, the operating unit of Oslo-listed Norse Atlantic ASA, petitioned Agder District Court for bankruptcy on 27 Nov, hours after lessors moved to end leases on all its Boeing 787-9s. It said it could not raise enough short-term funding. The parent and UK unit are not part of the filing and are exploring options.
stories.why: Jet fuel costs tied to the Middle East war are pushing thinly funded long-haul airlines out, cutting low-fare transatlantic capacity.

stories.h: US Air Force orders 15 more KC-46 tankers from Boeing for $2.8B
stories.sum: The award, posted on 24 Nov, covers Lot 13, the last under the fixed-price contract signed in 2011, with work due by the end of June 2030. Boeing has 203 KC-46s under contract including foreign sales and has delivered 116 to the US Air Force. Up to 75 more could follow under an extension, starting with Lot 14.
stories.why: Moving past the original fixed-price deal lets Boeing seek higher prices on future tankers, though the Air Force wants key flaws fixed first.

stories.h: Qantas set to give Boeing most of a 20-jet widebody order, Bloomberg reports
stories.sum: Qantas is set to order 20 long-range jets, mostly Boeing 787s plus some Airbus A350s, Bloomberg reported on 27 Nov, citing people familiar. Qantas said it is still talking to manufacturers and no decision has been made. The order is separate from 12 A350-1000ULRs, the first due in April 2027, as A380s retire by 2028.
stories.why: A win would bolster Boeing's 787 order book against the A350 as airlines renew long-haul fleets.

stories.h: Vanke asks bondholders to vote on 8 Dec on a second delay for a 1.2B yuan note
stories.sum: China Vanke wants to push back repayment of about 1.2B yuan ($180M) of a note due 15 Dec by another three years, its second extension on the bond, with a vote set for 8 Dec. Sources say any upfront cash payment may be well below the 40% paid in the first extension.
stories.why: Repeated extensions at a developer backed by state-owned Shenzhen Metro test how far Beijing will go to avoid a default.

stories.h: Malaysia has 186,318 unsold new homes from launches since 2020, PropLaunch says
stories.sum: The units are worth an estimated RM105.3B to RM230B and include 42,619 from projects launched from July to October; at the current sales pace they would take about 39 months to clear. Official data show third-quarter launches jumped 70.3% to 19,642 units, yet only 7.1% sold, and loan approval rates are the lowest since 2021.
stories.why: A swelling stock of unsold homes leaves developers facing pressure to slow launches or cut prices.

stories.h: Singapore condo resale prices hit a record as Huttons flags the most supply since 2013
stories.sum: SRX data show condo resale prices rose 1.3% in October from September and 3.8% from a year earlier to a record, though volumes fell 5.9% to about 987 units. Huttons expects up to 12,613 new private homes across 27 projects in 2027, the most since 2013, and prices up 2% to 5%.
stories.why: A wave of new launches could cap price gains just as resale values peak, shifting bargaining power toward buyers.

stories.h: US proposes 20% tariff on Singapore and 18% on Malaysia in excess-capacity probe
stories.sum: USTR proposed Section 301 duties on 14 economies on 25 Nov, including 20% for Singapore, 18% for Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia, 35% for Vietnam and 15% for Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and the EU. Semiconductors and patented drugs already under Section 232 are exempt. Comments are due 5 Jan, with a hearing on 25 Jan.
stories.why: The duties would largely replace levies the Supreme Court struck down in February, hitting exporters beyond the exempt chip sector.

stories.h: Malaysia tells firms to shun US-blacklisted buyers as Washington targets chip diversion
stories.sum: Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 27 Nov that companies were directed not to trade with US-blacklisted entities after a Cabinet briefing on chip export curbs. On 23 Nov the US listed Singapore-based Megaspeed International and six affiliates in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand over suspected diversion of Nvidia chips to China, which Megaspeed denies.
stories.why: Malaysia and Singapore, which is reviewing its own rules, must convince Washington their data centres are not routes to China.

stories.h: Malaysia sues Google over YouTube content; Anwar says US$15B investment is safe
stories.sum: Regulator MCMC filed two suits against Google LLC seeking a combined RM600M, alleging YouTube failed to remove content on gambling and scams and republished videos. Anwar Ibrahim said on 27 Nov, after speaking to Alphabet's Ruth Porat, that Google's planned US$15B of data-centre investment in 2027 and 2028 would not be affected.
stories.why: Malaysia is testing whether it can enforce its Online Safety Act on big platforms without scaring off data-centre investors.

stories.h: KLCI gains 2.1% on the week; ringgit seen holding between 4.10 and 4.13 per dollar
stories.sum: The FBM KLCI rose 1.16% to 1,589.24 on Friday, its fourth straight gain, for a weekly rise of 2.1%. The ringgit slipped to 4.1190 per dollar from 4.1105 a week earlier, and Kenanga expects it to trade between 4.10 and 4.13 next week. Singapore's STI rose 0.66% to 4,995.23.
stories.why: Asian rebounds are lifting Malaysian blue chips, but expected Fed hikes are keeping the dollar firm against the ringgit.
